title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 194 (Relation between principal and person duly appointed by agent to act in business of agency)

content.overview: Section 194 provides that where an agent, holding an express or implied authority to name another person to act for the principal in the business of the agency, has named another person accordingly, such person is not a sub-agent, but an agent of the principal for such part of the business of the agency as is entrusted to him.
content.glance: Where an agent has authority to name another person to act for the principal and does so, that person is not a sub-agent but an agent of the principal for the part of the business entrusted to him.
content.study: Where an agent, holding an express or implied authority to name another person to act for the principal in the business of the agency, has named another person accordingly, such person is not a sub-agent, but an agent of the principal for such part of the business of the agency as is entrusted to him. Current-law framing: distinction between a sub-agent and a person named by an authorised agent who becomes an agent of the principal.

examples.title: Authorised naming
examples.body: Agent has authority to name another person to act for the principal and does so. That person is an agent of the principal (not a sub-agent) for the entrusted part of the business under Section 194.

hypotheticals.question: Agent has authority to name another person to act for the principal and names that person. Is the named person a sub-agent?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Under Section 194 such person is not a sub-agent, but an agent of the principal for such part of the business of the agency as is entrusted to him.
